planets.name: Mercury
planets.curiosity: A day on Mercury (sunrise to sunrise) lasts 176 Earth days, which is twice its year.

planets.name: Venus
planets.curiosity: Venus spins backward compared to most planets, so the Sun appears to rise in the west and set in the east.

planets.name: Earth
planets.curiosity: Earth is the only known planet with stable liquid water on its surface.

planets.name: Mars
planets.curiosity: Mars has Olympus Mons, the tallest known volcano in the solar system.

planets.name: Jupiter
planets.curiosity: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant storm that has been active for centuries.

planets.name: Saturn
planets.curiosity: Saturn is so low in density that it would float in a giant enough ocean of water.

planets.name: Uranus
planets.curiosity: Uranus rotates on its side, with an axial tilt of about 98 degrees.

planets.name: Neptune
planets.curiosity: Neptune has the fastest winds in the solar system, reaching over 2,000 km/h.
